body_html:
Father’s Day messages in Spanish are often a little less sentimental than Mother’s Day messages, and a little funnier, but they still matter. Whether you are writing to your own dad, a Spanish-speaking father-in-law or a friend celebrating his first Father’s Day, el Día del Padre falls on the same day in the United States and Mexico: the third Sunday in June. Below are thirty-five messages for your dad, grandfather, father-in-law and the new dads in your life, with English translations.

Quick answer
  • Basic: ¡Feliz Día del Padre!
  • For your dad: Gracias por todo, papá. Eres mi héroe.
  • For your father-in-law (formal): Feliz Día del Padre, suegro. Gracias por todo.
  • In the US, Father’s Day is the third Sunday in June, the same as in Mexico.
{{toc}}

Short Father’s Day messages in Spanish

  1. ¡Feliz Día del Padre!
    Happy Father’s Day!
  2. ¡Feliz día, papá!
    Happy day, Dad!
  3. Gracias por todo, papá. Eres mi héroe.
    Thank you for everything, Dad. You’re my hero.
  4. Feliz día al mejor papá del mundo.
    Happy day to the best dad in the world.
  5. Te quiero mucho, pa.
    I love you lots, Dad.
  6. Gracias por estar siempre.
    Thank you for always being there.

Pa and papi are affectionate short forms. In Mexico, many adults still call their father papá or apá in casual speech.

Heartfelt messages for your dad

  1. Gracias por enseñarme con tu ejemplo, no solo con tus palabras.
    Thank you for teaching me by example, not just with words.
  2. Todo lo bueno que hay en mí lo aprendí de ti.
    Everything good in me, I learned from you.
  3. Gracias por trabajar tanto para que no nos faltara nada.
    Thank you for working so hard so we never went without.
  4. Aunque no lo diga seguido, te admiro mucho.
    Even if I don’t say it often, I admire you a lot.
  5. Eres el hombre que siempre quise ser.
    You’re the man I always wanted to be.
  6. Ahora que soy papá, te entiendo mejor y te quiero más.
    Now that I’m a dad, I understand you better and love you more.
  7. Gracias por tus consejos, incluso los que no te pedí.
    Thank you for your advice, even the advice I didn’t ask for.
{{image:2}}

For your grandfather, father-in-law and new dads

  1. Feliz Día del Padre, abuelito. Gracias por tantas historias.
    Happy Father’s Day, Grandpa. Thank you for so many stories.
  2. Feliz Día del Padre, suegro. Gracias por recibirme en su familia.
    Happy Father’s Day, father-in-law. Thank you for welcoming me into your family. (formal)
  3. Al papá de mis hijos: gracias por ser tan buen papá.
    To the father of my children: thank you for being such a good dad.
  4. ¡Feliz primer Día del Padre! Tu bebé tiene mucha suerte.
    Happy first Father’s Day! Your baby is very lucky.
  5. Feliz día a todos los papás de la familia.
    Happy day to all the dads in the family.
  6. Feliz día, tío. Siempre fuiste como un segundo papá.
    Happy day, Uncle. You were always like a second dad.

For more on in-laws, see {{link:talking-to-your-in-laws-in-spanish|talking to your in-laws in Spanish}}.

Funny Father’s Day messages

  1. Gracias por enseñarme todos tus chistes malos. Ahora los cuento yo.
    Thanks for teaching me all your bad jokes. Now I tell them.
  2. Feliz Día del Padre al único que sabe dónde está el control de la tele.
    Happy Father’s Day to the only one who knows where the TV remote is.
  3. Papá, prometo no tocar el termostato hoy.
    Dad, I promise not to touch the thermostat today.
  4. Feliz día al rey de la parrilla.
    Happy day to the king of the grill.
  5. Gracias por todos los “pregúntale a tu mamá”.
    Thanks for all the “ask your mom”s.
{{book:a-road-in-bloom}}

For a dad who is no longer here

  1. Hoy te recuerdo con más cariño que nunca, papá.
    Today I remember you more fondly than ever, Dad.
  2. Te extraño, pero sigues en todo lo que hago.
    I miss you, but you’re still in everything I do.
  3. Gracias por todo lo que me dejaste. Feliz día hasta el cielo.
    Thank you for everything you left me. Happy Father’s Day up in heaven.

Hasta el cielo (all the way to heaven) is a common and gentle way to send a message to someone who has died.

How the day is celebrated

In Spanish-speaking families in the United States, Father’s Day usually means a family meal, often a carne asada in the backyard or a trip to a favorite restaurant, and the kids make cards at school. Mexican families celebrate on the same Sunday, so relatives on both sides of the border are celebrating at the same time. One exception to know about: if you have family in Spain, they celebrate on March 19, the feast of San José.

If your partner’s family is celebrating, a simple question opens the door: ¿Qué hacen para el Día del Padre? For a family meal, see {{link:family-dinner-spanish-phrases|Spanish phrases for family dinner}}, and for congratulations in general, {{link:congratulations-in-spanish|congratulations in Spanish}}. The Diccionario panhispánico de dudas explains why holiday names like Día del Padre are written with capital letters.

{{image:3}}

Tips and common mistakes

  • Feliz día de padre. Use the article: Feliz Día del Padre.
  • Mixing up dates. In the US and Mexico, it is the third Sunday in June. Only Spain celebrates on March 19.
  • Papá vs papa. Without the accent, papa means potato. See {{link:spanish-accent-marks|Spanish accent marks}}.
  • Too formal with your own dad. With your own father, tú is normal in most families; usted is for some older or very traditional families.
{{quiz}}

Final thoughts

Father’s Day messages in Spanish can be heartfelt, funny or both. Pick one that sounds like your relationship, and send it on the third Sunday in June. For more family moments, see {{link:spanish-phrases-for-everyday-situations|Spanish phrases for everyday situations}}.

faq.q: How do you say Happy Father’s Day in Spanish?
When is Father’s Day for Spanish-speaking families in the US?
faq.a: The third Sunday in June, the same day as in Mexico. Only Spain is different, celebrating on March 19.

faq.q: What is a short Father’s Day message in Spanish?
faq.a: Gracias por todo, papá. Te quiero mucho.

faq.q: How do I write to my father-in-law on Father’s Day?
faq.a: Warmly and politely, often with usted: Feliz Día del Padre, suegro. Gracias por todo.
